tagline.text: A port city in western Leyte with a seaside promenade and a university campus

location.label: Location
location.text: Central west coast of Leyte Island, a port city facing the Camotes Sea

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800~2,500 (per person, day trip or 1 night, based on transport from Ormoc or Tacloban, meals and lodging)

children.text: Baybay City is a port city on Leyte's west coast and the second-largest city in Leyte by area after Ormoc. The Baywalk and Veteran's Park, where people gather in the evening, the Immaculate Conception Church completed in 1870 and the Visayas State University (VSU) campus are the core of a day trip.

Baybay is a component city on the central west coast of Leyte Island, facing the Camotes Sea to the west. According to Wikipedia its area is 459.30 square kilometers, the second largest in Leyte after Ormoc, and its 2024 population is 114,708. It borders Albuera to the north, Inopacan to the south, and Burauen, La Paz, MacArthur, Javier, Abuyog and Mahaplag to the east. The east is mountainous and the land slopes down toward the west coast, with an average elevation of about 147 m and a highest point of 1,313 m. Most residents speak Cebuano and Boholano with some Waray influence, and the original local language, Baybayanon, is spoken in five barangays: Guadalupe, Gabas, Kilim, Patag and Pangasugan. About 90 percent of the population is Catholic. The city has 92 barangays, 23 of which are urban zones (Poblacion Zones 1 to 23). It was once the most populous town in Leyte, and today it is a commercial center for western Leyte, with banks, restaurants, cafes and shops.

The area was originally called Pangasugan, and the name is said to come from a local resident's answer when a Spanish expedition asked the name of the place: "Ang suba nagbaybay sa Pangasugan" ("the river runs along the shore toward Pangasugan"). Wikipedia says Baybay was probably the only settlement on Leyte's west coast known to Magellan's expedition. In 1620 Jesuits from Carigara established a presence, and on September 8, 1835 a parish was created under Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, becoming an independent parish on February 27, 1836. A fire in 1866 destroyed most of the town, leaving only the Holy Cross chapel standing. In 1899 the American coast guard temporarily closed the port, hitting the copra and hemp trade hard. In February 1901 American forces arrived, and Filipino forces led by Florentino Peñaranda fought in the area before surrendering. Japanese forces occupied the town in 1942–1944 and left on October 19, 1944, and the liberation forces used Baybay as a base for patrols toward Ormoc. It became a city on June 16, 2007 under Republic Act 9389, and after back-and-forth Supreme Court rulings its cityhood was affirmed on February 15, 2011.

The first place most travelers visit is the seaside Baywalk and Veteran's Park. Wikipedia says this is the most visited area, especially at night. Local guides describe the Baybay City boardwalk, the "Pantalan," as a major attraction where you can buy local food. The Immaculate Conception Church is the center of Catholic life in Baybay's old town. The first church was built in Barrio Punta, and the present church was begun in 1852 and finished in 1870. Some guides also mention the Archdiocesan Shrine of Saint Anthony de Padua, but there is little information on its location and opening hours, so check locally.

The university and nature also make a day. Visayas State University (VSU) is known as one of the larger agricultural universities in the Philippines by land area, and a guide says it began in 1924 as the Leyte Agricultural School. It is recognized by the Department of Tourism (DOT) as a tourist site, has resorts and convention facilities and a 180-degree view of Mount Pangasugan and the Camotes Sea, and is nicknamed the "Resort University." Lintaon Peak hiking, the "Eastern Sea of Clouds" and Ayas Hill are also introduced as viewpoints with entrance fees, but little information is available on prices and access. There are also said to be pleasant green forest paths at the foot of Mount Pangasugan. For any of them, it is safest to ask the city tourism office or your lodging before you set out.
A stretch of seaside promenade and park that is the most visited place in Baybay. It is described as especially busy at night. Avoid quiet spots late in the evening.
Described as a boardwalk near the port where you can buy local food. Little information is available on hours and facilities, so check locally.
The Catholic church of Baybay City, begun in 1852 and finished in 1870. It is the center of the Binaybayon Festival on December 27, honoring the city's patroness.

A large agricultural university campus recognized by the DOT as a tourist site. It is known for its 180-degree view of Mount Pangasugan and the Camotes Sea. Check the visitor rules at the university office.

children.text: Introduced as mountain-view hiking spots. Entrance fees are mentioned, but there is little information on amounts and directions. Set out in the morning with a guide.
Baybay is a major port on central west Leyte with boats to Cebu and elsewhere. Overnight ferries run to Cebu City 3 to 6 days a week depending on the operator (2026 guides; days change often).

These include the Binaybayon Festival on December 27, the Tigbawanon Festival on the second Saturday of January, the Sirong Festival on June 13 and the Halaran Festival in October. Dates may change from year to year, so check with the city hall.

As of 2026 guides, Lapulapu Shipping (8 PM departure, 3 to 6 days a week) and Roble Shipping (9 PM departure, 3 to 4 days a week) run overnight boats between Cebu City and Baybay, taking about 5 to 7 hours. The basic seat (economy) fare is about
, depending on operator and class, and may rise with fuel surcharges. Days and times change often.
There is also news of another operator resuming the Cebu–Baybay route, so check current service with the operator.

Baybay has a Corona Type IV climate with no clearly defined dry or rainy season and is generally wet. Even so, mountain hikes and seaside walks are better from December to May. The main festivals fall on December 27, the second Saturday of January, June 13 and in October.
According to modeled climate data, annual rainfall is about 1,598 mm, with February the driest month and June to October the wettest. Average daily highs are 28–30°C and lows are 22–25°C.

Budget lodging is mostly family-run guesthouses at about ₱400 to ₱1,200 a night. Wikivoyage lists J.R. Pension House with fan rooms at ₱200~250 and air-conditioned rooms at ₱500, but that is an old source, so be sure to check current prices. For mid-range, Baybay City Hotel is mentioned, and upscale facilities are rare, with one guide suggesting Tacloban as the alternative.

The main industries in Baybay are farming and fishing, with rice, corn, abaca, root crops, fruit and vegetables. There are also cottage industries such as bamboo and rattan crafts, ceramics, mat weaving and furniture making, so you may find handicrafts at the market. The city has the Western Leyte Provincial Hospital, Baybay Doctors' Hospital and VSU Hospital in case of an emergency. It is also an education city, with the Franciscan College of the Immaculate Conception and the Acedilla Technological Institute Foundation alongside VSU, and Baybay National High School, opened in 1945, is described as the oldest and largest high school in the city. The postal code is 6521 and the area code is 053.

The food is mostly Filipino seafood and street food. There is a simple eatery inside Prince Supermarket in town, and Metrobank and PNB on Magsaysay Avenue are said to have 24-hour ATMs. At the market you can buy fruit and coconut snacks.
The Baywalk is busiest at night. Go around sunset and stay into the evening.
The VSU campus is large and hard to cover on foot. Decide where you are going and check the entry rules at the office.
Start mountain hikes such as Lintaon Peak early in the morning and find a guide.
